routes.description: Establish Christian theism as more plausible than skeptical agnosticism through a cumulative case from cosmic fine-tuning and origin, objective morality, the resurrection and Christian revelation, and experiences of numinous beauty, while accounting for evolutionary suffering and the absence of coercive proof.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the converging considerations are reasonably explained by a loving, orderly creator and specifically support Christian commitment, with the evidential force of the whole exceeding the skeptical alternatives and the counterevidence from suffering and uncertainty.

motionBridge.description: Show that the combined evidence makes Christian theism more plausible than skeptical agnosticism.

centralBridges.description: Connect cosmic existence and life-permitting physical constants to an intelligent, orderly creator rather than an unexplained or multiverse alternative.
Connect historical resurrection claims and revelation to Christianity rather than merely generic creator theism.
Show that morality and beauty reinforce the scientific and historical considerations as a cumulative case despite uncertainty.
Explain why evolutionary and physical suffering remain compatible with a loving God who creates through stable natural laws.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend rational commitment on substantial but noncoercive evidence rather than requiring mathematical proof.
Explain how divine purposes may operate through physical, evolutionary, and neural mechanisms without competing with them.

routes.description: Establish skeptical agnosticism as the more warranted position by showing that the concept of God and the proposed evidence underdetermine Christian theism, that fine-tuning admits reversal or alternatives, that resurrection and public-revelation claims lack sufficient historical support, and that extensive suffering weighs against a loving creator.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the named considerations remain mysteries or support multiple explanations rather than preferentially supporting Christianity, especially when the improbability of apparently avoidable suffering under loving-creator theism is included in the comparative assessment.

motionBridge.description: Show that the total evidence does not warrant preferring Christian theism to skeptical agnosticism.

centralBridges.description: Show that disputed or incomprehensible divine attributes prevent the evidence from identifying the Christian God with adequate confidence.
Show that narrow physical constraints may be unexpected under omnipotent creation and do not uniquely favor a creator.
Show that extensive apparently avoidable evolutionary suffering is more expected under naturalism than under a loving creator.
Show that source-critical uncertainty and limits on private revelation weaken the move from generic possibility to Christianity.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Preserve naturalistic, evolutionary, legendary-development, and other rival explanations for the cited phenomena.
Distinguish acknowledging profound mysteries and existential stakes from claiming that they justify confident belief.

sections.title: Fine-tuning, cosmic explanation, and divine power
sections.rationale: This issue contains the principal scientific case for an intelligent creator and the central skeptical challenge that physical fine-tuning may constrain or count against an omnipotent God, including multiverse and ultimate-explanation alternatives.

sections.title: Evolutionary suffering and orderly creation
sections.rationale: The comparative expectations of naturalism and loving-creator theism turn substantially on animal suffering, predation, extinction, and physical evil, together with the claim that stable natural laws and divine purposes explain their presence.

sections.title: Resurrection, Christian revelation, and historical warrant
sections.rationale: The resurrection and revelation are required to move the case from generic theism to Christianity, while Gospel source criticism, legendary development, martyrdom claims, Pauline testimony, and the public limits of private experience bear on that move.

sections.title: Morality, beauty, and transcendent experience
sections.rationale: Objective moral experience and numinous beauty provide distinct proposed signs of transcendence, while biblical moral concerns, aesthetic diversity, emotional and evolutionary accounts, and skeptical concessions define their comparative evidential reach.

sections.title: Cumulative evidence, uncertainty, and warranted commitment
sections.rationale: The debate ultimately compares a cumulative rationale for noncoercive Christian commitment with agnostic restraint toward several acknowledged mysteries, making standards of proof, conceptual clarity, combined evidential force, and existential significance burden-relevant.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: God provides evidence sufficient for free personal commitment rather than coercive mathematical proof that would make belief unavoidable.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-05.proposition: The universe's beginning and fine-tuning, objective moral experience, beauty, and the failure of strict atheism jointly make trust in God reasonable.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: Life-permitting physical constants require explanation, and an intelligent creator is more plausible than an empirically inaccessible multiverse while also addressing why anything exists.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: God creates through orderly laws, and God's desire for loving relationships guides the selection of physical parameters capable of producing complex creatures.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Evolution's suffering is compatible with a God of order because an elegant lawful creative process can be providentially directed without repeated supernatural interventions.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Physical suffering follows from stable natural laws, and avoiding it would require continual divine intervention that would compromise God's ordered creation.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Historical testimony, the empty tomb, resurrection appearances, and witnesses' costly persistence make Jesus's bodily resurrection the most likely explanation.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Cross-cultural recognition of good and evil points beyond evolutionary explanation toward a holy source of goodness and love.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: The New Testament's sweeping portrayal of Jesus and its resurrection case can rationally compel commitment without resolving every textual dispute or attaining proof.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: Experiences of numinous beauty and musical longing can provide fleeting indications of a transcendent reality that ordinary natural description may miss.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-01.proposition: Agnosticism is warranted because God's nonexistence cannot be established, while the observed world still supplies reasons to doubt a traditional creator.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-07.proposition: Christianity conflicts with the moral intuitions invoked as evidence for God because biblical treatments of slavery and women generate serious moral objections.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-09.proposition: Fine-tuning may count against creator theism because an unconstrained God should not require life to depend on a narrow physical knife edge or hostile meta-conditions.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Physical constants are not logical necessities, so claiming that God could not produce a life-permitting universe under different constants poses a genuine challenge to divine omnipotence.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Immense and apparently unnecessary evolutionary suffering is expected under atheistic naturalism but surprising under a loving creator intending relationship with human beings.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Unknown divine reasons for suffering permit an equivalent appeal to unknown natural explanations for fine-tuning, while less agonizing lawful ecosystems show that animal suffering was avoidable.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Resurrection appearances are better explained as legendary development because the earliest form of Mark lacks them and later sources supply increasingly elaborate accounts.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: Personal revelation could raise an individual's belief in God, but private experience has little force as public evidence and intellectual argument cannot be the only accessible route to faith.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-01.proposition: The diversity of objects and experiences called beautiful makes it difficult to infer a single intrinsic maximum of beauty resembling God.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-06.proposition: Fine-tuning, suffering, beauty, and the resurrection remain profound mysteries that do not justify confident conclusions about God's existence.
